about: The motion deck: moves this engine can already make, each with its numbers. Dealt by engine/tools/deck.mjs so two films do not reach for the same three. A dealt card is a prompt to consider, in the film's own subject and medium: keep it, adapt it, or drop it and say why. Times are seconds, distances are fractions of the frame's width, so every card holds at any size and frame rate. Each card's aka lists the everyday names people use for it; calls maps names to engine calls that are not cards; refused lists names anidoodle will not make, with the reason and what to make instead. deck.mjs find resolves a name against all three.

roles.workhorse: carries a film quietly, safe to use twice
roles.accent: noticed when it happens, once or twice
roles.signature: can be the one move that is this film's own, used at the open, the middle and the close

moves.move: Frame 0 is already composed and already moving: the film opens partway into a camera move or an action, never on a still that then starts.
moves.build: A path camera whose move began before frame 0 (camera.ts, path: (f) => move(f + lead)), or a cycle opened at phase 0.3, so the first second has travel in it.
moves.not: A piece that draws itself: there the empty page is the opening.

moves.move: The film opens through a round opening that grows from the thing it is about, 0.5 to 0.8 s, evenly in log space so it does not crawl then snap.
moves.build: iris(ctx, env, seam(f, 0, len), blank, scene, { center }) in transitions.ts; shape "blot" for an inked film.
moves.not: Centred on nothing. Or when the close also irises and a seam in the middle does: the third one is a preset.

moves.move: Open so close on one detail (an eye, a hand, a nib) that the subject is not yet readable, then pull back over 1.5 to 3 s until it is.
moves.build: A dolly back: Camera zoom keys from 4 to 6 down to 1 with monoZoom: true; divide stroke widths by cam.weight(cam.at(f)) so the close-up reads close, not enlarged (camera.md).
moves.not: A detail that was not drawn to be seen at that size. Check the first frame at --scale 2.

moves.move: No establishing shot: the first frame is the middle of the action, and the wide shot comes second, as the answer to where we are.
moves.build: Order the shots action, then wide; the score enters on frame 0 with one sound that has a reason.
moves.not: A calm piece, or a subject the viewer cannot name from the close shot within a second.

moves.move: A hard cut hidden in travel. The outgoing shot accelerates over 0.2 to 0.4 s, its last frame is its fastest, the incoming shot opens at the same speed in the same direction and comes to rest over 0.8 to 1.4 s.
moves.build: matchedMove({ dir, exitDist, exitF, entryF }) in seams.ts, added to each scene's camera look; hold it with checkSeam. Render with --blur auto.
moves.not: Either shot has no room to travel, or the two travel different ways. Then both sides come to rest and it is a plain cut on a beat.

moves.move: The camera flies into the outgoing shot and comes out in the next: a push of about 1.2 over 0.2 s, the cut, then the incoming shot growing from about two thirds of its size to rest over 0.5 s.
moves.build: matchedZoom({ push, exitF, entryF }) in seams.ts multiplies each camera's zoom; the incoming scene must be painted wider than the frame, because it opens small.
moves.not: The thing flown into is not what the next shot is about. Then it is a push laid over a join.

moves.move: One object crosses the seam untouched while the world changes round it: same screen position, same size, same colour on the last frame of one scene and the first of the next.
moves.build: Drive it from one function of the absolute frame that both scenes call (relay in motif.ts); checkRelay holds the two sides to 2 px.
moves.not: The object has no reason to be in the second scene. A mascot that only watches is decoration.

moves.move: A shape in the outgoing picture travels, stretches a little while moving, and becomes a shape of the next picture, landing on it exactly.
moves.build: handoff({ from, to, t0, t1 }) in morph.ts; coverShape when the target is the whole page; checkShapes at the landing.
moves.not: The two shapes share nothing the eye can follow (colour, edge, a rough outline). A morph between strangers is a wipe.

moves.move: One item out of a set is chosen and grows until it is the next scene; the next scene's first frame is framed exactly like the item.
moves.build: A camera punch-in that does not come back (launchGallery.ts); frame the incoming scene's first frame from the card's box.
moves.not: The set was only built to be left.

moves.move: Something already in the scene grows until it covers the frame, and when it clears the next scene is there. The next scene is complete underneath on every frame.
moves.build: coverShape (morph.ts) on the scene's own shape, or the bloom in launchCut.ts; close it on the next picture's focal point.
moves.not: An arbitrary shape brought in to hide the join, or the third time in one film.

moves.move: A loaded brush is pulled across in the direction the story is already moving, wet ink running ahead of the new picture, 0.6 to 0.9 s.
moves.build: brushWipe(ctx, env, p, from, to, { angle, ink }) in transitions.ts.
moves.not: A clean, set register. Or more than twice.

moves.move: A plain hard cut with both sides at rest, on a strong beat, between two frames that match in one thing: a shape, a position, a direction of gaze.
moves.build: No call (and not seam-matched-cut, which hides the cut in travel). Put the cut frame on the cue table's downbeat and check the pair as stills: one thing sits in the same place on both.
moves.not: Nothing matches, or the music has no beat there. Then use the gentle move.

moves.move: The scenes sit side by side in one layout larger than the frame and the camera travels between them; the route says how they relate.
moves.build: One Camera for every plane (camera.ts); world-placed scenery so the view changes all the way (koiWorld.ts, webTour.ts).
moves.not: The places are unrelated, or the trip between two stops is long and empty.

moves.move: A thing leaves the way it came, mirrored in time and shorter: what arrived over 0.5 s on a settling curve leaves over 0.25 s on an accelerating one, along the same path.
moves.build: Run the entrance's own progress backwards through easeIn (seams.ts); if it was revealed from behind an edge it tucks back behind that edge where the edge is now.
moves.not: The exit is the point of the scene. Then it gets a move of its own.

moves.move: The sound crosses the cut ahead of the picture or behind it: the next scene is heard 0.3 to 0.8 s before it is seen (a J-cut), or the last scene is still heard 0.5 to 1.5 s into the next (an L-cut). The ear makes the join before the eye does.
moves.build: Cue the incoming scene's first sound at CUT minus the lead in the SfxPlan (filmSfx cues are film frames), or let the outgoing scene's sound run past CUT with lengthS; the score can enter its next section a beat early (music/sound-design.md, Sound across a cut).
moves.not: A hit or a contact: its sound belongs on its own frame, and one that trails its picture reads as lag.

moves.move: A hold that is never still: the camera pushes in 3 to 6 percent over the whole shot, so a quiet shot still changes every second.
moves.build: Two Camera keys, zoom 1 to 1.04, ease "linear" for this one move only: an eased drift stops at both ends and the stop is the dead air.
moves.not: A shot with a lot of its own motion. Two moves at once fight.

moves.move: The camera travels sideways and depth does the work: near things swing wide, far things barely stir, and something crosses the lens in front of the subject.
moves.build: One Camera, planes at z from -0.3 (across the glass) to 4 or more (camera.md, depth planes). Never a hand-set drift per layer.
moves.not: A flat style whose point is the flatness (a print, a diagram).

moves.move: The camera follows a moving subject a little late: the subject pulls ahead when it accelerates and the frame catches up when it slows, so speed is felt.
moves.build: A path camera: path: (f) => ({ look: subject(f - lag), zoom }) with lag of 0.1 to 0.2 s; lead room in front of the subject.
moves.not: The subject must stay pinned for a read (a face, a label).

moves.move: One impact rings through the frame: full strength on the hit, gone within a beat, with a little rotation.
moves.build: cam.shake({ from, to, amp, seed, rot }) in camera.ts; amp is screen px, 0.8 to 1.5 percent of the width.
moves.not: More than two a film, or on anything that is not a real contact.

moves.move: The camera pulls back and the thing we were looking at turns out to be a small part of something larger.
moves.build: A dolly out: Camera zoom keys (eased in log2), monoZoom: true, 1.5 to 3 s; the large thing is painted in the world from the start, never faded in at the end.
moves.not: The larger thing adds nothing to the story. Then it is only a pull-back.

moves.move: Attention moves from one thing to another in the same frame without the camera moving: the first dims and softens its edges, the second gains contrast and line weight.
moves.build: Draw both from one emphasis value 0..1: stroke weight, saturation and value contrast (no ctx.filter, the contract forbids it).
moves.not: The two things are in different places in the story. That is a seam.

moves.move: A fast pan to a new subject inside one scene that decays to rest on it: the last third of the move is the slow part.
moves.build: Camera key with ease "out" over 0.4 to 0.7 s; keep the peak under speedCeiling(W, fps) (seams.ts) and render with --blur auto.
moves.not: Past the ceiling. Then cut on the beat instead.

moves.move: The moment of realisation: the subject keeps its size in the frame while the world behind it stretches away (or closes in), over 1 to 2.5 s, slow enough to be felt before it is noticed.
moves.build: dollyZoom((f) => cam.at(f)) in camera.ts, used as a path camera, on a dolly of 1.6 to 3 times; the subject on the hero plane and at least two planes behind it at real depths (camera.md, Lens and dolly).
moves.not: Fewer than two depth planes (with nothing behind the subject nothing visibly happens), or a beat that is not a realisation. Once a film.

moves.move: The thing is drawn into the picture in the order a hand would make it, the tool visible, each stroke taking the time its length asks for.
moves.build: kind: "drawing" and the style plate's own draw order (workflows/drawing-process.md).
moves.not: A fade standing in for drawing. If it cannot be drawn on, it arrives some other honest way.

moves.move: A thing comes out from behind something already in the picture (a hill, a card's edge, another figure), so the picture supplies the mask.
moves.build: Clip with the occluder's own outline (pathShape in morph.ts) and move the thing out from under it on a settling curve, 0.4 to 0.7 s.
moves.not: A mask in mid-air with nothing drawn where its edge is.

moves.move: The scene is there from the first frame but dark; light arrives (a door, a sun, a lamp) and the subject is found by it.
moves.build: Paint the lit and unlit values of every surface and mix them by distance from the light's edge as it moves.
moves.not: A style with no light in it (flat vector, a diagram).

moves.move: Parts arrive from the back to the front, each held above the stack with a wide soft shadow that closes as it lands, 0.08 to 0.12 s apart.
moves.build: paperCraft.ts is the worked example; no more than about seven parts in flight at once.
moves.not: Parts that are not real parts of the subject.

moves.move: A number changes while the thing it counts is changing, and stops on the frame the action stops. Never after.
moves.build: Drive the digits and the action from the same progress value (productUI.ts counts values this way).
moves.not: A figure that is not true of the data on screen.

moves.move: A line is written by its tool, one stroke after another, at the speed of a hand, and holds long enough to be read twice.
moves.build: writeOn or sentence in kinetic.ts; on its own frame, or over a calm area where the frame would pass as a poster (workflows/launch-video.md, Type).
moves.not: Over a face, the focal detail or busy texture. In doubt the line gets its own frame.

moves.move: One line hands over to the next word by word, so there is never more than one full line on screen: the old line's words leave at twice the pace they came.
moves.build: sentence() in kinetic.ts for the arriving line; run the leaving line's word progress backwards at half the entry stagger; the new line's first word starts on a beat.
moves.not: Lines that must be compared. Those stay together.

moves.move: A dot lands on one thing, a line is drawn out from it, a short label is written at its end; the dot follows the thing, the label holds still.
moves.build: drawCallout in callout.ts, pinned with cam.toScreen; one or two on screen.
moves.not: The picture is busy where the label would sit and a backing would cover something that matters.

moves.move: A label on one scene travels across the seam and lands as the heading of the next, on that scene's first frame.
moves.build: A callout with handoff (callout.ts); the next scene draws it with drawLabel at the same pose; checkHandoff holds it to 2 px.
moves.not: The label's words are not what the next scene is about.

moves.move: The one word that matters is underlined by hand after the line has landed, 0.25 s, on a beat. Underlined, never struck through.
moves.build: caption(..., "underline") in kinetic.ts, started when the line's progress reaches 1.
moves.not: More than one word a line, or more than twice a film.

moves.move: The world stops on a telling pose and a name or a word is written by hand beside it; the camera keeps creeping in while it is written, then time picks up exactly where it stopped.
moves.build: A speed 0 key in timeRemap (timeRemap.ts) whose keepsMoving names the writing; writeOn in kinetic.ts and a slow push, both on the film's own frame; hold for as long as the word takes to write plus one beat to read it.
moves.not: Nothing is written or moving during the stop (dead air, and timeRemap refuses it), or a calm film where a hard stop is a jolt.

moves.move: Before any large action the body goes the other way first: a crouch before a jump, a draw back before a throw, 0.15 to 0.3 s, a quarter of the action's size.
moves.build: A held pose keyed before the action and blended through (a rig's mix between poses); bones keep their length (anatomy.md).
moves.not: A machine, or a move meant to startle.

moves.move: Loose parts arrive late and go further: a tail, hair, a sleeve follow the body by 0.05 to 0.1 s a segment, each segment wider than the one before.
moves.build: Sample the driving angle at f - lag * i down the chain and scale its swing by 1 + 0.15 to 0.2 * i.
moves.not: A stiff material. Wood and metal do not whip.

moves.move: Nothing stops dead. A thing that lands goes a little past, comes back, and is at rest by 0.3 to 0.5 s; weight decides how far past.
moves.build: One overshoot of 4 to 8 percent then a decay on easeOut; heavier things overshoot less and take longer.
moves.not: Type meant to be read while it lands, and anything in a clean set register that should simply arrive.

moves.move: In a run the body works hard and the head rides level: the eyes stay on one line while the spine folds and opens under them.
moves.build: Solve the neck last, to a head height that does not follow the body (hold the head to a few px through a stride).
moves.not: A bounce that is the joke (a toy, a rubber-hose character).

moves.move: A character at rest is alive: the chest rises over 3 to 4 s, a blink of 0.1 to 0.15 s every few seconds at uneven gaps, an ear or a tail answers a sound.
moves.build: Periodic over the loop length so the seam closes; blink times from rng(seed), never a fixed interval.
moves.not: A portrait whose stillness is the point.

moves.move: A contact is shown where it happens: dust, a splash or a compressed shadow on the frame of the hit, clearing over 0.4 to 0.8 s.
moves.build: Seeded particles born on the contact frame from the contact point; the sound effect cued to the same frame (music/sound-design.md).
moves.not: A touch with no force in it.

moves.move: The subject's action moves something else in the scene a moment later: grass bends in the wake, birds lift, water rings spread.
moves.build: Drive the secondary thing from the primary's position at f - delay, falling off with distance.
moves.not: A reaction that draws the eye off the subject at the moment that matters.

moves.move: After the biggest change in the film the result is held, alive but unbroken, for 1 to 2 s before anything else happens.
moves.build: A hold in the cue table after the payoff with only breathing motion in it (cam-slow-push, act-blink-and-breathe).
moves.not: A loop under 6 s, where the hold would be most of it.

moves.move: At the top of the action (the peak of a jump, the instant before contact) time slows and stays slow long enough to read the shape, then gathers back into real time. The score keeps its own tempo throughout.
moves.build: timeRemap in timeRemap.ts: ease down over 0.2 to 0.35 s to a speed of 0.2 to 0.4, hold 0.5 to 1.2 s, ease back over 0.3 to 0.6 s; draw the scene at t.at(f) (it must draw between its frames) and cue the contact sound at t.filmFrameOf(contact) (camera.md, Time).
moves.not: Nothing is in flight, a loop (a remap changes how much scene time the film covers, so the loop stops closing), or a second time in one film: the second slow motion halves the first.

moves.move: The last frame is the first frame, earned: the film ends where it began and the viewer now knows what it means.
moves.build: Draw the closing shot from the opening shot's own function at the same frame; for a loop, verify-export.mjs --loop holds the last frame to frame 0.
moves.not: A film whose point is that things changed for good.

moves.move: The ending takes things away: motion slows, parts leave, the music stops on a bar line, a breath of near silence, then one soft sound on the last picture.
moves.build: A section with fewer parts and no low drum, then one resolved note; music.mjs check prints the ARC line, which flags an ending that out-shouts the film.
moves.not: A sting of a few seconds, which is all ending.

moves.move: The thing that travelled through the film lands as part of the mark, and the end card opens from it.
moves.build: handoff (morph.ts) from the actor's last shape to the mark's shape; the wordmark written after it lands (logo in kinetic.ts).
moves.not: A mark the actor does not resemble in any way.

calls.call: iris(ctx, env, p, from, to, { center, shape })
calls.use: A round opening from a point or closing to one; open it from what the next scene is about (motion-grammar.md, Three ready-made seams).

calls.call: flashCut(ctx, env, local, cut, from, to)
calls.use: A hard cut under a short burst of light, on a strong beat; declare the film's flashes to checkFlashes.

calls.call: Camera keys with lens (a true lens zoom), or dollyZoom
calls.use: A lens zoom magnifies every plane by one factor and changes no parallax; to move closer through the world, key the dolly (zoom) instead (camera.md, Lens and dolly).

calls.call: cam.shake({ from, to, amp, seed, rot, freq }) over a long window
calls.use: A long low shake with a little rotation and a low freq reads as a hand on the camera; keep amp small (camera.md, Shake).
Subframes per frame from each frame's measured speed, averaged in linear light; the film's own code is untouched.
Characters appear on a typing cadence with a caret, one tick sound per character (music/sound-design.md).

calls.call: timeRemap([{ f, speed, ramp }]) with speed above 1, or your own falling time
calls.use: Speed above 1 runs the scene fast; timeRemap never runs time backwards, so for a rewind draw the scene at a falling time yourself, scene(g, t0 - (f - f0)), which the contract allows (camera.md, Time).

calls.call: onTwos: true in the film's meta
calls.use: Each drawing is held for two frames, the rhythm of paper and stop-motion; motion blur leaves it alone (formats.md).

calls.call: the gentle move: a bloom, a card flip, a push, the card growing into the scene
calls.use: The standard seam when no designed one clearly fits (motion-grammar.md, the default does not change).

refused.name: glitch
refused.why: Colour split and torn pixels are a template overlay with no cause in the picture; they read as stock, not as a made mark.
refused.instead: a cut on the beat (seam-cut-on-beat), or one shake on a real impact (cam-impact-shake)

refused.name: light sweep
refused.why: A shine sliding across chrome is a stock overlay; nothing in the picture casts it.
refused.instead: reveal-by-light: the light belongs to the world and finds the subject

refused.name: fade-in
refused.why: Marks are made, not faded or scaled up from nothing: a fade standing in for drawing is a tell on the craft bar.

refused.name: particle burst
refused.why: A burst on everything is decoration with no force behind it, so it is never a default.
refused.instead: emph-contact: dust or a splash born on a real contact, from the contact point

refused.name: cross dissolve
refused.why: Two copies of one thing, each half there, read as a ghost; between unrelated pictures a dissolve is a slideshow join. A poster-frame dissolve and a reduced-motion fallback are the exceptions (formats.md, interactive.md).
refused.instead: seam-shape-becomes or seam-actor-carries (move one object, change what it is mid-trip); between unrelated scenes, the gentle move

refused.name: lens flare
refused.why: Lens artefacts (flare, light leaks, bokeh discs) painted onto a drawing read as stock overlays, not as light.
refused.instead: one named light in the scene (realism-and-craft.md), or reveal-by-light
